title: Image content
description: The `image` content block, carrying base64-encoded data and its MIME type.
question: Does an image result survive adaptation, or is it dropped or flattened to text?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: A dropped image block is a silent failure: the call succeeds, the result arrives, and the payload the tool existed to return is simply gone.

notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: a result without `structuredContent` comes back unchanged, image block intact. For a result that carries `structuredContent`, every content block is dropped, images included; only the structured value reaches the agent.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: a lone image block reaches the model as an `input_image` item. When a result has several blocks the SDK stringifies the whole content array into one text item, so an image beside other kinds arrives as JSON text.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: with the default `result_mode="text"`, `Tool.acall` returns the image block as the MCP content object when the result has no text (direct: `y`). In a `dspy.ReAct` run the observation the model reads is that object's Python repr, `«type='image' data='...' mime_type='image/png' ...»` (react: `a`). When a result carries any text block, `_convert_mcp_tool_result` returns the text alone and drops the image block at both boundaries.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: The default `McpToolExecutor` result converter accepts text blocks only. Any `image` block makes it throw `Unsupported content type: "image"`: the direct executor raises it as a `RuntimeException`, and AiServices turns it into an error tool result the model reads in place of the block. A result with `structuredContent` never reads its blocks at all.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcpTool.Run` returns `{"output": text}`, where `formatMCPContent` replaces the block with a placeholder line (`[MCP image: mimeType="image/png", size=70 bytes]`, with no image data), and the model receives that map as `FunctionResponse.response`. When the result also has `structuredContent`, as in the mixed result, `Run` returns `{"output": structuredContent}` and the block is dropped.
notes.ms_agent_framework_dotnet: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): a lone image block becomes a `DataContent` with its bytes and MIME type at both boundaries. Beside `structuredContent` (`mixed_content`) `McpClientTool` returns the `CallToolResult` as JSON, so the image reaches the model as base64 characters inside a text result, not as an image.
